description:
Put an image into CraterView.ai. Every image goes in this way first: the tools that run a job, and quote, take the `input_key` this answers with. It runs nothing and charges nothing.

Give one of:
- image_url, for an image already online.
- content_type and content_length, for a file on this computer that your shell can read. The answer has a `curl` command that sends it straight to storage, and the file is there once that has succeeded.
- job_id, for the file a finished job returned.
- image_base64, only for a very small file you cannot send any other way.

Call this without asking for a link the user gave you. A file on the user's computer stays there until they say to run: read its width and height in your shell and give those to quote. An `input_key` can be sent to any number of jobs, and the file is deleted a day after it was made.

If you cannot send the image, because you can only see it in this conversation or your shell cannot reach storage, ask the user for a link, or to choose the photo at https://craterview.ai/app and give you its File ID, which is an `input_key`.

Privacy: images and results are private to the account, never used to train, tune or evaluate a model, public only if the user submits them to the gallery.

content_length.description: For a file on this computer, with content_type: its exact size in bytes, read in your shell so the image never enters your context. The limit is 300MB.

content_type.description: For a file on this computer, with content_length: the file's type.

image_base64.description: The image itself, base64-encoded; a data: URL is also accepted. Limit 8MB decoded. Only for a very small file you cannot send any other way: inline base64 is text in your context, and a one-megabyte image costs hundreds of thousands of tokens. An image you can only see in this conversation cannot be sent: encode the file's bytes, never what you see.

image_url.description: A public or signed http(s) link to a PNG, JPEG, WebP, HEIC, HEIF or TIFF image, which is fetched from there. The limit is 300MB.

job_id.description: The `id` of a finished job whose result is the image, to run another job on what it returned. For enhance_photo, the original photo is strongly recommended: it might not work well on a result.

name: upload_photo
